MEG study of the spatiotemporal and hemispheric organization of happy-face recognition, comparing emotion discrimination with face/hand categorization and happy with neutral faces.

Within-participant task experiment in 16 analyzed volunteers. Emotion and categorization blocks were counterbalanced, as were response-button assignments. A separate reaction-time study was conducted later in ten of the analyzed participants.

Twenty volunteers participated in MEG; four were excluded for noisy signals or large head movements, leaving sixteen for analysis. Ten of these sixteen also participated in a later reaction-time study.
